ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the vertical axis is concentration, and the horizontal axis is time (s), labeled with about 30, 60, and 90 s. The three curves are labeled I, II, and III respectively; curves I and II start from near 0, rise, and gradually become flat, while curve III starts from a higher concentration, decreases, and has already basically become flat near 60 s. Reasoning: The reaction is 2NO2(g) ⇌ 2NO(g) + O2(g), and initially there is only NO2, so the only curve in the figure that starts from an initially high concentration and decreases, curve III, corresponds to NO2. By t = 60 s, curve III is horizontal, indicating that [NO2] no longer changes with time. When the temperature is unchanged, the forward reaction rate depends on the concentration of the reactant NO2; since [NO2] remains constant at 60 s, the forward reaction rate also remains constant.

raw_record.question_text:
$NO_2$ gas is placed in a sealed, evacuated container and allowed to decompose via the following equation:

$2NO_2(g) \leftrightarrow 2NO(g) + O_2(g)$

The graph below indicates the change in concentration for each species over time. At t = 60 s, how is the rate of the forward reaction changing?

method.method_draft: Identify NO2 as the only initial reactant from the equation and match it to the graph curve that decreases from an initial concentration, curve III. At t = 60 s, observe that curve III is flat, so [NO2] is constant. Since the forward rate depends on [NO2] and temperature is not changing, conclude that the forward reaction rate is remaining constant.

Interpret this as the reaction mixture having reached dynamic equilibrium. 图像描述：图中横轴是时间 Time(s)，纵轴是浓度 Concentration(M)。三条曲线中，一条从较高浓度下降后在约 60 s 前后变成低而平的曲线；另外两条从 0 上升，并在约 60 s 时也都变成水平平台。也就是说，在 t = 60 s 附近，NO2、NO 和 O2 的浓度曲线都基本不再变化。
